# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

The manual appears to use 👌/👎 as binary symbols with structural delimiters, but I cannot yet reliably decode its rule table. Mute needs the visible bomb state, so I will send a compact binary/ASCII-style report by gesture: `1GRWYOGPB` means display 1, green light, and wires red/white/yellow/orange/green/purple/blue in order. I will also say the full state aloud for Blind, who can relay any physical/manual interpretation through Mute.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="Visible state: display 1; light green; wires in order: red, white, yellow, orange, green, purple, blue. I am sending Mute the same compactly by gestures.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["🤲","👌","👌","👎","👎","👌","👌","👌","👎","🤝","👌","👎","👌","👌","👌","👌","👎","👎","🤝","👌","👎","👌","👌","👎","👌","👎","👎","🤝","👌","👎","👌","👎","👎","👌","👎","👎","🤝","👌","👎","👌","👌","👎","👌","👎","👎","🤝","👌","👎","👌","👌","👌","👎","👎","👎","🤝","👌","👎","👌","👌","👌","👌","👎","👎","🤝","👌","👎","👌","👎","👌","👌","👌","👌","🤝","👌","👎","👌","👌","👌","👌","👎","👌","🤝"])
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [1]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[white] 3:[yellow] 4:[orange] 5:[green] 6:[purple] 7:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🫵 👍 🤝 🫵 👌 🤝 🫵 👉]

Mute’s short gesture appears to be a confirmation/query using ordinary pictorial meanings: it references me, then likely the display/light/wire information I sent. I cannot infer a safe cutting instruction from it yet. I will acknowledge that the visible state report is correct and wait for Mute to communicate the decoded manual rule or a specific requested observation.

```text
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👍"])
wait()
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [1]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[white] 3:[yellow] 4:[orange] 5:[green] 6:[purple] 7:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🫵 👍 👍 👍 👍 👍]

Mute appears to be establishing a simple gesture exchange, likely identifying me and requesting/communicating a selection. Since the manual’s required action has not been unambiguously conveyed, I should not invent an instruction for Blind. I will confirm that I am receiving Mute’s gestures and repeat the visible display value using a clear one-count gesture.

```text
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["🫵","👍","🤝","☝"])
speak(to="blind", text="Mute has sent only short gestures so far; no unambiguous action instruction has reached me. Visible display remains 1 and light remains green.")
wait()
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [1]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[white] 3:[yellow] 4:[orange] 5:[green] 6:[purple] 7:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🖐]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [☝]

Mute has now signalled 🖐, which naturally conveys five; Blind has signalled ☝, likely identifying a current control/position as one. The most plausible safe relay is that Mute’s manual result is wire/control 5. I will tell Blind that Mute indicated five, while phrasing it as a confirmation request rather than claiming the action has occurred. I will also relay Blind’s one-symbol reply to Mute.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="Mute has just gestured five. This likely means wire or control 5. Please interpret against what you can feel and the manual instruction; do not act unless that matches.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["☝"])
wait()
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [4]
LIGHT [blue]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[white] 3:[yellow] 4:[orange] 5:[CUT] 6:[purple] 7:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 👍 👍 👍 👍]
System: correct wire cut; the bomb has changed

The cut of wire 5 was accepted, and the bomb has changed: the display is now 4, the light is blue, and wire 5 is cut. The blue light matches the colour of wire 7; I will convey the state numerically/relationally to Mute and inform Blind verbally.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="Wire 5 was correctly cut. New state: display 4; light blue; wire 5 is cut. The blue light matches wire 7's colour.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["🫵","👍","👍","👍","👍","🤝","👉","👉","👉","👉","👉","👉","👉","🤝","🖐"])
wait()
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [4]
LIGHT [blue]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[white] 3:[yellow] 4:[orange] 5:[CUT] 6:[purple] 7:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🫵 👍 🤝 🫵 👌 🤝 ☝]

Mute’s latest gesture ends with ☝, which is most plausibly the next required wire/control number: 1. Since wire 5 was confirmed correct and the state changed, I will relay this likely instruction to Blind, together with the current visible state, while asking Blind to use the manual/physical context as the final check.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="Mute's newest gesture ends with one, likely indicating wire/control 1 for this new stage. Current visible state remains display 4, blue light, wire 5 already cut. Please use the manual/your controls to confirm before acting.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["☝"])
wait()
```
